bug_semantics: When createVerifier is configured with a stateful RegExp carrying the global (/g) or sticky (/y) flag in allowedAud, allowedIss, allowedSub, allowedJti, or allowedNonce, fast-jwt retains that RegExp object and repeatedly calls its test() method. A successful test advances RegExp.lastIndex, so the next otherwise identical verification can fail and reset it, producing alternating acceptance/rejection of valid tokens. This is an availability-only logical denial of service; it does not make invalid tokens pass.
flaw_origin: The initial verifier implementation treated every object exposing test() as a stateless claim matcher and returned the same object from ensureStringClaimMatcher. verifyPayload then invoked that retained matcher for every token without normalizing RegExp.lastIndex. Commit 51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 first added both the unsafe matcher reuse and its repeated test() call; its direct parent contains no src/verifier.js or equivalent vulnerable implementation.
ai_marker: absent — BIC commit object author and committer are both Shogun <shogun@cowtech.it>; the complete commit message is "feat(wip): Initial version." and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/security/advisories/GHSA-3j8v-cgw4-2g6q identifies npm package fast-jwt, affected range < 6.2.1, first patched version 6.2.1, the five allowed* options, /g and /y statefulness, and rejection of valid rather than acceptance of invalid tokens.

First-party fix PR https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/pull/593 states that ensureStringClaimMatcher returned RegExp objects directly and validateClaimValues repeatedly called test() without resetting lastIndex, causing alternating PASS/FAIL; it describes resetting lastIndex before every match.

BIC https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/commit/51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 added src/verifier.js. Its ensureStringClaimMatcher at https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/blob/51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790/src/verifier.js#L6-L12 returns r unchanged whenever r.test is a function, and verifyPayload at https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/blob/51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790/src/verifier.js#L40-L68 executes allowed.some(a => a.test(value)). Source history/blame traces these original vulnerable operations to this commit, making it the smallest public BIC rather than a later refactor.

Direct-parent verification: `git show -s --format='%H %P' 51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790` gives sole parent 5063678a36ff118da9671f1f1df3d67cc95d1169. The parent tree https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/tree/5063678a36ff118da9671f1f1df3d67cc95d1169 has no src directory, and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nearform/fast-jwt/5063678a36ff118da9671f1f1df3d67cc95d1169/src/verifier.js returns 404; therefore the vulnerable matcher and sink are absent from the immediate parent.

Boundary check: vulnerable v6.2.0 still returns test-capable objects unchanged in https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/blob/v6.2.0/src/verifier.js, while patched v6.2.1 wraps RegExp and sets r.lastIndex = 0 before r.test(v) in https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/blob/v6.2.1/src/verifier.js. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 v0.1.0` returned 0, proving the BIC predates the first published tag; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 18d25904e4617e8753526d1b3ab5a2cccdea726a v6.2.1` returned 0, proving the fix is included at the patched boundary.

Direct fix https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/commit/18d25904e4617e8753526d1b3ab5a2cccdea726a changes src/verifier.js so actual RegExp instances are wrapped and lastIndex is reset to zero immediately before every test; its added tests exercise repeated calls for /g and /y across the affected allowed* claims. Release boundary: https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/releases/tag/v6.2.1.

reasoning: The advisory-defined failure is caused by persistent JavaScript RegExp state, so the causal lines are the matcher-normalization code that preserves a caller's RegExp object and the validation sink that repeatedly calls test(). History places both in the initial source commit 51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790; the sole direct parent has no verifier source, directly proving absence rather than relying only on blame. The BIC is already an ancestor of v0.1.0, consistent with the advisory's all-versions-before-6.2.1 range. Fix 18d25904e4617e8753526d1b3ab5a2cccdea726a directly removes the state leak by resetting lastIndex for each RegExp test and is an ancestor of v6.2.1. Inspection was restricted to the BIC commit object for attribution: it has a human author/committer and no AI marker or trailer, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
